def: briefly, i.e. (in time) speedily, or (in manner) rapidly

occurrences.text: So that servant came, and shewed his lord these things. Then the master of the house being angry said to his servant, Go out quickly into the streets and lanes of the city, and bring in hither the poor, and the maimed, and the halt, and the blind.
And he said, An hundred measures of oil. And he said unto him, Take thy bill, and sit down quickly, and write fifty.
The Jews then which were with her in the house, and comforted her, when they saw Mary, that she rose up hastily and went out, followed her, saying, She goeth unto the grave to weep there.
But I will come to you shortly, if the Lord will, and will know, not the speech of them which are puffed up, but the power.
I marvel that ye are so soon removed from him that called you into the grace of Christ unto another gospel:
But I trust in the Lord Jesus to send Timotheus shortly unto you, that I also may be of good comfort, when I know your state.
That ye be not soon shaken in mind, or be troubled, neither by spirit, nor by word, nor by letter as from us, as that the day of Christ is at hand.
Lay hands suddenly on no man, neither be partaker of other men’s sins: keep thyself pure.
Do thy diligence to come shortly unto me:
